prompt: A web server needs to query a database in order to build its response. At that instant, what is it?
hint: The roles describe the moment of the conversation, not the equipment. Who starts the conversation with the database?

choices.text: The database's client, because it is the one starting that request — and it is still a server in the conversation with the browser.
choices.why: The roles belong to the moment: the same machine can be a server in one conversation and a client in another, at the same time.

choices.text: It stays purely a server, because a machine configured as a server cannot take on another role.
choices.why: The configuration decides which programs it runs, not which role it holds in each conversation.

choices.text: It becomes an intermediate host, a category distinct from client and server.
choices.why: `Host` is the neutral term for any machine with an address, not a third role in the conversation.

choices.text: Neither, because the query happens inside the same local network and the roles do not apply.
choices.why: Distance changes nothing: whoever asks is the client, whether the other side is in the next rack or on another continent.

prompt: Match each term to what it describes. There are options left over in the right-hand column.
hint: Two of these terms describe a role in a conversation; one describes the machine, regardless of what it is doing.

pairs.right: The one who starts the conversation and makes the request
The one who waits to be asked and returns the answer
Any machine with an address on the network
The number saying which program the data is meant for

right_distractors: The physical cable joining two neighbouring machines
The program that translates domain names into addresses
